q: The side of a square wire loop is $0.20\,\text{m}$, and the loop is perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0.50\,\text{T}$. How large is the magnetic flux through the loop?
The magnetic flux through a coil grows, is at its greatest at the moment $t_1$ and then begins to decrease. How large is the induced voltage in the coil at the moment $t_1$?
a: Zero. At the greatest value the flux graph $(t, \Phi)$ is horizontal for a moment, so the rate of change of flux $\Delta\Phi : \Delta t$ and the voltage $e = -N \cdot \Delta\Phi : \Delta t$ are zero. A large flux does not mean a large voltage.
